paper_title: Shuttle Between the Instructions and the Parameters of Large Language   Models
caption: : The induction performance of SHIP and SFT on SNI with respect to the number of observed samples. The accuracy is the average accuracy over all seen and unseen tasks.
model_annotation: This plot illustrates the induction performance of two methods, SHIP and vanilla SFT, by displaying accuracy with respect to the number of observed samples. The x-axis is labeled "observed samples" and uses a linear scale ranging from 1 to 6, with numeric tick marks spaced at regular intervals of 1. The y-axis is labeled "accuracy" and employs a linear scale with visible tick marks spaced at intervals of 0.1 from 0.4 to 0.8, although the plotted data extends slightly below and above these visible bounds. The plot contains two lines, both featuring solid line styles and circular markers. The line representing SHIP is green and maintains a relatively steady trajectory across the x-axis; it begins at an accuracy of approximately 0.81 at 1 observed sample, exhibits a minor decline to roughly 0.79 at 4 observed samples, and reaches its highest point of approximately 0.82 at 6 observed samples. The line representing vanilla SFT is blue and demonstrates an overall upward trend; it starts at a value of roughly 0.33 at 1 observed sample, increases to 0.37 at 2 samples where it remains flat through 3 samples, and then continues to rise steadily, concluding at a peak value of approximately 0.45 at 6 observed samples.
